capabilities.notes: Turns the place being searched into a point, so a question naming only a town can be answered. Without it the only way to bound a search was a commute destination, and a question with no commute returned nothing at all while reporting that it had been efficient about it.
Turns a named place into a point once, for the whole search. The distance from every listing to it is then arithmetic on coordinates already in hand, so the check itself costs nothing.

One call per page. The plan emits a single op and the executor repeats it while the response reports more pages, up to max_fanout, because the page count is data and the plan is written before any of it exists. The free predicates cut the page count as well as the candidate count: the unfiltered San Jose pool is 20 pages, the filtered one is a single page. A listing price is stable over days rather than hours, and the six hour life it had before meant a second question about the same city an hour later paid for the whole candidate set again, which is the opposite of what the ledger is for. Forty eight hours, and the interface shows the real age of every fact either way.

One detail call per surviving listing. Expensive, so it runs last and only on survivors.
Never prunes. Returns place_results.gps_coordinates for the office address in one call.

travel_mode is an integer on this engine: 0 driving, 1 cycling, 2 walking, 3 transit. directions[] returns route alternatives and the first is not always the fastest, so the verdict takes the minimum duration across them. duration is already in seconds and distance in meters. Prunes with slack only: a listing can be nearer the destination than its own centroid. Measured 28 Aug 2026 over 20 answers: coverage 0.80 and selectivity 0.44, once cells are fitted to the listings rather than laid over the box.

google_local ignores ll and answers for the wrong city. google_maps with type=search honours it and carries operating_hours per weekday, which is what makes an opening time answerable rather than a guess. Measured 28 Aug 2026 over 40 answers: coverage 0.45 and selectivity 0.94. Slack leaves more than half its answers undecided and it rules almost nothing out, so its elimination power is close to zero and the planner is right to leave it out unless the candidate set is very large.

selectivity_prior of 1 because it never prunes. area_signal is always soft. The region name comes from the candidate search response, not from the bounding box, so this cannot run until listings have been found. Filtering by lookback_days uses iso_date, which is present on every result.
